parameters.name: table
parameters.description: The table to iterate over. Can be a physical table or a table expression like FILTER().
parameters.examNote: Every row of this table is visited once. Use FILTER() here to limit the rows before iteration.

parameters.name: expression
parameters.description: Evaluated in the context of each row. Typically arithmetic combining multiple row-level columns.
parameters.examNote: This expression runs in row context — it can access the current row's column values like a calculated column formula.

returnType: Decimal (sum of all per-row expression results)
summary: SUMX iterates every row of a table, evaluates an expression per row, and sums the results. Use it when the value you need to sum does not already exist as a column — for example, multiplying Qty × UnitPrice per row.

examples.label: Revenue = Qty × Unit Price per row

iteratorFlow.description: SUMX visits each row of the Sales table, computes Qty × UnitPrice in that row's context, then sums all intermediate results.

commonTraps: SUM(Sales[Revenue]) only works if Revenue is already a stored column. Use SUMX when you need per-row arithmetic that doesn't exist in the model.
SUM(Sales[Qty]) * SUM(Sales[UnitPrice]) is mathematically wrong — it multiplies totals, not per-row values.
CALCULATE inside the expression argument triggers context transition, converting each row context into a filter context.

sqlEquivalent.note: SQL can inline arithmetic directly inside SUM(). In DAX, if a Revenue column doesn't exist in the table, SUM(Sales[Revenue]) fails. SUMX computes the per-row expression on the fly — equivalent to writing the formula inside SQL's SUM().
